text:
maria: heads-up — overnight reconcile in us-west-2 shifted gpupool AZ allocations, bumped one AZ to 70% of nodes. Not an outage but observable imbalance and a couple of failed pod schedules. cc @sam @lee

sam: ugh, any idea what triggered reconcile? tf apply or controller loop?

maria: controller reconcile loop. noticed because autoscaler couldn't place some GPUs; logs show our gpupool module got a changed `az_affinity` computed value after KMS rotation.

lee: can you paste the plan? might be the module default changed after we promoted the new provider alias.

maria: snippet from the reconcile run: ```
# computed change (no user intent)
module.gpupool.aws_autoscaling_group.this: 
  - azs: ["us-west-2a", "us-west-2b"] -> ["us-west-2a", "us-west-2b", "us-west-2c"] (forces replace)
```

harper: hmm. that looks like a drift detection + autoscale reaction. Did gitops CI run a `terraform apply` or was this reconciler acting directly? :thinking_face:

infra-bot: reconcile-controller detected drift at 2026-03-17T03:14:22Z (run id rc-20260317-03). Action: plan-only by default; subsequent automated apply triggered due to `auto_remediate=true` tag.

sam: where did `auto_remediate` come from? that's usually false for gpupools.

maria: it was introduced by a module refactor in tf-mod-gpupool-v3 two weeks ago (PR #482). The module had a new default for `allow_autoremediation` to true to help small infra teams, and we didn't override it in our stack.

lee: that explains the behaviour. Two follow-ups: 1) revert default or explicitly set `allow_autoremediation = false` in our overlay; 2) add a preflight check in the reconcile controller to block AZ-expanding changes that would cause immediate ASG replace.

harper: agree. Also we should add a safety gate in GitOps: require PR approval + CI plan review for any module version bump that touches `az_affinity` or `instance_count`.

sam: cost impact? we briefly spun up extra instances and some spot interruptions happened while ASG replaced. rough delta ~ $1.1k for the window (short-lived), but potential risk for larger autoscale.

maria: logged cost alert and notified finance. Also, KMS key rotation earlier that night caused provider alias refresh which cascade-updated computed fields in tf state.

lee: small mitigation: pin module to v2.7.1 in our overlay and create a canary stack in us-west-2a only to validate module upgrades for gpupool. Then we can roll forward v3 after fixes.

maria: I'll open the pin PR. Also adding a short-term reconciler toggle: `prevent_az_expansion=true` to block AZ list length increases until we verify rollout logic.

harper: please include a runbook step to manually drain nodes in the affected AZ and migrate training jobs. Add an incident note so oncall doesn't scramble if it recurs.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline: opened pipeline run pipeline/9321 to pin module and set `allow_autoremediation=false` in overlay. Please review. :shipit:

sam: thanks — once PRs merge, let's monitor gpufleet health dashboard for 24h and set a short alert to catch AZ skew > 15%.

maria: will do. PR link: https://git.example.com/redwood/infra/merge_requests/549 — includes pin + reconciler toggle + runbook link.

lee: can we also add a unit test in the module CI that simulates provider alias/key rotation and ensures computed lists don't flip unexpectedly?

maria: good call, adding test story to the PR.

harper: nice postmortem-lite thread. next steps assigned: maria (PR + runbook), lee (canary plan + module CI test), sam (monitoring + cost note).
